purpose: Teach: 変質/崇高/安堵/慰謝/感知/講ずる/発病/成就

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 桜さん、戦時下に人格が変質した兵士の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Sakura, you wrote a paper about how soldiers' personalities changed under wartime stress, right?
lines.style: Warm, conversational opening. Gentle confirmation phrased as a question, inviting Sakura in. Steady eye contact. Teacher checking understanding, not interrogating.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、宗教者の崇高な献身を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I focused on the noble sacrifice and devotion of religious figures in my paper.
lines.style: Slight uncertainty underneath the surface politeness. A careful correction, testing whether the teacher will follow. Speaking clearly but with a hint of defensiveness.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 戦後の安堵感を表現した文学を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And you explored postwar literature that captured the relief and healing people felt afterward?
lines.style: Thoughtful, slightly less certain. Phrased as gentle confirmation rather than statement. A slight pause before speaking, as if recalling. Genuine curiosity about Sakura's direction.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、被害者への慰謝料制度を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I actually examined the compensation systems set up to support victims.
lines.style: Another quiet correction. Patient but definite. Not challenging, just clarifying her actual focus. Slight emphasis on the substance of her work, not the teacher's assumption.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 感知できない放射線リスクを論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: So you covered the invisible risks of radiation exposure in another one?
lines.style: Warm interest returning. Less tentative now—teacher adjusting to the pattern. Leaning forward slightly, genuine engagement. Phrased as a sincere question.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、災害時の対策を講ずる行政手順を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—but my focus was on how governments actually respond during disasters.
lines.style: Matter-of-fact but respectful. Sakura settling into her rhythm. Each correction is becoming easier. Confident without arrogance. Direct eye contact.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 戦時下の集団発病の歴史を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: And the history of mass illness outbreaks during wartime—that was another topic?
lines.style: Teacher matching Sakura's rhythm now. Softer, more collaborative. A genuine question, not a prompt. Respecting the pattern Sakura has established.

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: はい、社会運動が成就するまでの過程を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes—I traced how social movements actually gain momentum and succeed over time.
lines.style: Clear, confident. Sakura has found her footing. She's no longer correcting—she's sharing. Final statement carries quiet pride. Slight ease in her shoulders, warm closing.
